$comment: Deno configuration for the Edge Functions, and the reason CI can lint them at all.
eslint.config.js ignores this directory ('Deno runtime, separate lint pass') and the
package's lint script was `echo "linted by Deno, not eslint"`. No Deno pass existed,
so the worker — which holds the service-role key, makes the outbound fetch, and is the
SSRF surface — was the one part of the tree with no lint coverage at all. Wiring it up
immediately found a dead `deno-lint-ignore-file no-explicit-any` at the top of
worker/index.ts covering zero `any`s, which is a small thing and exactly the kind of
small thing an unlinted file accumulates.
Tests are excluded on purpose rather than out of convenience. They run under Vitest on
Node, not on Deno: they import from 'vitest', they never touch a Deno global, and
`pnpm test` already covers them. Linting them here produced 33 require-await errors
against async interface fakes and nothing else.
require-await is excluded for the same reason one level up. It fires on exactly three
things — stubSummaryProvider.generateSummary, stubEmbeddingProvider.embed and
disabledImageProvider.generateArtwork — all of which implement an interface whose real
implementation calls a network API. They are async because the contract is async, not
because they happen to await something; the point of the stub set is that a fresh clone
with no API key runs the same pipeline through the same shapes. Dropping `async` would
change the declared return type and `return Promise.resolve(x)` is the same thing said
less clearly. The rule targets a real mistake; here it only ever finds a deliberate
interface implementation.
